papers.title: PEPTiGEN: a tool for mining antimicrobial resistance PEPTides using GENe data of public available repositories
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Detecting antimicrobial resistance (AMR) remains challenging due to the complexity and evolution of resistance mechanisms. Liquid chromatography online coupled to tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) offers a promising diagnostic tool. Its success, however, depends on an up-to-date database which can be used to target AMR specific peptides. Results We present PEPTiGEN, a computational tool that automatically generates tryptic peptides for any prokaryotic gene and its variants. PEPTiGEN was validated both in silico and in vitro , showing 99% accuracy compared to manually generated tryptic peptides and 98% compared to experimental mass spectrometry data. To demonstrate its potential, we used PEPTiGEN to generate the first AMR peptide database by screening publicly available nucleotide AMR sequences using the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD). Together, PEPTiGEN and the AMR peptide database are cornerstones for advancing LC-MS/MS applications in AMR detection and clinical diagnostics. Availability The PEPTiGEN code and AMR peptide database are publicly available at github ( https://github.com/ftabaro/inspection ) and Zenodo ( https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21196702 )
papers.abstract:
MOTIVATION: Detecting antimicrobial resistance (AMR) remains challenging due to the complexity and evolution of resistance mechanisms. Liquid chromatography online coupled to tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) offers a promising diagnostic tool. Its success, however, depends on an up-to-date database which can be used to target AMR specific peptides.

RESULTS: We present PEPTiGEN, a computational tool that automatically generates tryptic peptides for any prokaryotic gene and its variants. PEPTiGEN was validated both in silico and in vitro, showing 99% accuracy compared to manually generated tryptic peptides and 98% compared to experimental mass spectrometry data. To demonstrate its potential, we used PEPTiGEN to generate the first AMR peptide database by screening publicly available nucleotide AMR sequences using the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD). Together, PEPTiGEN and the AMR peptide database are cornerstones for advancing LC-MS/MS applications in AMR detection and clinical diagnostics.

AVAILABILITY: The PEPTiGEN code and AMR peptide database are publicly available at github (https://github.com/ftabaro/inspection) and Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21196702).

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

papers.llm_research_question_zh: 动机：由于抗性机制的复杂性及其不断演变，检测抗菌素耐药性仍然是一项具有挑战性的任务。
llm_highlights_zh: 液相色谱与串联质谱联用技术（LC-MS/MS）是一种极具前景的诊断工具。
然而，其成功与否取决于是否拥有一个最新的数据库，该数据库能够用于筛选针对耐药菌特异性肽段的药物。
结果：我们开发了PEPTiGEN这一计算工具，该工具能够自动为任何原核生物基因及其变异体生成胰蛋白酶消化后的肽段序列。
papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
由于抗性机制的复杂性及其不断演变，检测抗菌素耐药性仍然面临诸多挑战。液相色谱与串联质谱联用技术为这一领域提供了有力的诊断工具，但其应用效果取决于是否拥有能够识别特定耐药肽段的最新数据库。  

**研究结果**  
我们开发了PEPTiGEN这一计算工具，它能自动为任何原核基因及其变异体生成胰蛋白酶消化后的肽段。该工具在体外及计算机模拟实验中均得到了验证：与人工生成的肽段相比，其准确率高达99%；与实际质谱数据相比，其匹配度也达到了98%。为了展示其实用价值，我们利用PEPTiGEN结合《综合抗生素耐药性数据库》中的公开序列信息，构建了首个用于检测抗菌素耐药性的肽段数据库。目前，PEPTiGEN代码及该肽段数据库均已公开发布在GitHub（https://github.com/ftabaro/inspection）和Zenodo平台（https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21196702）上。  

**结论**  
PEPTiGEN与所构建的抗菌素耐药性肽段数据库为推进液相色谱-串联质谱技术在耐药性检测及临床诊断中的应用奠定了重要基础。

然而，其成功与否取决于是否拥有一个最新的数据库，该数据库能够用于筛选针对耐药菌特异性肽段的药物。

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
由于抗性机制的复杂性及其不断演变，检测抗菌素耐药性仍然面临诸多挑战。液相色谱与串联质谱联用技术为这一领域提供了有力的诊断工具，但其应用效果取决于是否拥有能够识别特定耐药肽段的最新数据库。  

**研究结果**  
我们开发了PEPTiGEN这一计算工具，它能自动为任何原核基因及其变异体生成胰蛋白酶消化后的肽段。该工具在体外及计算机模拟实验中均得到了验证：与人工生成的肽段相比，其准确率高达99%；与实际质谱数据相比，其匹配度也达到了98%。为了展示其实用价值，我们利用PEPTiGEN结合《综合抗生素耐药性数据库》中的公开序列信息，构建了首个用于检测抗菌素耐药性的肽段数据库。目前，PEPTiGEN代码及该肽段数据库均已公开发布在GitHub（https://github.com/ftabaro/inspection）和Zenodo平台（https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21196702）上。  

**结论**  
PEPTiGEN与所构建的抗菌素耐药性肽段数据库为推进液相色谱-串联质谱技术在耐药性检测及临床诊断中的应用奠定了重要基础。

all_papers.primary_summary_raw:
MOTIVATION: Detecting antimicrobial resistance (AMR) remains challenging due to the complexity and evolution of resistance mechanisms. Liquid chromatography online coupled to tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) offers a promising diagnostic tool. Its success, however, depends on an up-to-date database which can be used to target AMR specific peptides.

RESULTS: We present PEPTiGEN, a computational tool that automatically generates tryptic peptides for any prokaryotic gene and its variants. PEPTiGEN was validated both in silico and in vitro, showing 99% accuracy compared to manually generated tryptic peptides and 98% compared to experimental mass spectrometry data. To demonstrate its potential, we used PEPTiGEN to generate the first AMR peptide database by screening publicly available nucleotide AMR sequences using the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD). Together, PEPTiGEN and the AMR peptide database are cornerstones for advancing LC-MS/MS applications in AMR detection and clinical diagnostics.

AVAILABILITY: The PEPTiGEN code and AMR peptide database are publicly available at github (https://github.com/ftabaro/inspection) and Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21196702).

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

all_papers.title: Antigen-sampling gut cells moonlight as organizers of immune defense
all_papers.summary: Microfold cells are known for ferrying gut antigens to immune cells to trigger antibody responses. We identify a second function for microfold cells in Peyer’s patches in establishing a spatial niche that positions group 3 innate lymphoid cells and sustains their production of the protective cytokine interleukin-22
